children.name: Personalised Wealth Advice
children.blurb: Personalised wealth advice uses AI to tailor portfolio construction to an individual's goals, constraints, tax situation, risk tolerance, and time horizon.

children.blurb: Portfolio optimisation beyond mean and variance moves past the Markowitz framework that uses only expected return and volatility.

children.name: Tail Risk Hedging
children.blurb: Tail risk hedging in AI portfolio construction is the practice of reducing exposure to rare but severe losses that can hit concentrated AI equity, credit, or venture positions.

children.name: Sustainability Factors in Portfolios
children.blurb: Sustainability factors in portfolios refer to environmental, social and governance criteria used alongside financial metrics when selecting and weighting assets, including AI-related instruments.

children.name: Pricing Illiquid Assets
children.blurb: Pricing illiquid assets covers positions that do not trade on an active exchange, such as private AI company equity, venture fund interests, restricted stock, intellectual property, data rights, and thinly traded tokens.

sections.body: Portfolio construction in AI economics is the practical use of machine learning to assemble and manage investment portfolios. It covers personalised advice, optimisation beyond mean and variance, tail risk hedging, sustainability factors, and pricing illiquid assets. Current work includes systems that read a client's stated goals and constraints and produce a proposed allocation, not a generic model portfolio. Optimisation routines now incorporate higher moments like skewness and kurtosis, and the site tracks 117 listed AI-related instruments with daily prices, which gives a concrete universe for that work. Tail risk hedging uses machine learning to estimate rare loss events from options and historical stress data. Sustainability factors are scored from company disclosures and news, and illiquid asset pricing uses comparable transactions and learned discount rates.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The field is uneven. Personalised advice is workable for simple goals but still struggles with incomplete client data and changing life events. Optimisation beyond mean and variance is mathematically mature, yet the honest limit is that estimated higher moments are noisy and unstable out of sample. Tail risk hedging remains unsolved in any reliable sense, because rare events are rare and models overfit to the last crisis. Sustainability factors are widely used but their definitions vary, and there is no agreed way to trade off carbon scores against returns without a client's own values. Pricing illiquid assets is the least solved, since there are few transactions and no clean price history, so any model output is a range, not a point.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The five pages form a sequence from client to asset. Personalised Wealth Advice is the entry point, showing how a system turns a person's situation into constraints and objectives. Portfolio Optimisation Beyond Mean and Variance then takes those objectives and builds the allocation, using the site's 117 listed AI-related instruments as a possible universe. Tail Risk Hedging sits next to optimisation, because it addresses what mean and variance miss, the rare losses that can wipe out a portfolio. Sustainability Factors in Portfolios adds a layer of non-financial preferences on top of the allocation, and Pricing Illiquid Assets closes the loop by explaining how to value the parts of a portfolio that do not trade daily. A reader would start with Personalised Wealth Advice, move to Optimisation, then consult Tail Risk Hedging for downside protection, Sustainability Factors for values, and Pricing Illiquid Assets for private holdings.
